In an earlier version, self-driving-car used to wait until an all-stop intersection was completely free from traffic before proceeding through. However, engineers found that when the car did that, other drivers [people] would ignore it and just go into the intersection. This 'inching into the intersection' thing was actually developed as a way to signal to other drivers that self-driving-car wanted to make a maneuver and was ready to do so. The inching is something real drivers do at intersections to signal this, and human drivers are primed to look for the inching. When self-driving-car wasn't doing it, human drivers didn't let it go in the intersection because they didn't think it was planning on moving.

Inflammation is the bodies defense against attacks (which is what yours thinks just happened to it). Basically your body does everything it can to stop the trauma or invader from gaining any ground so it sends as much blood to the area to kill anything that doesn't belong and heal the damaged tissue. The four parts of inflammation are:

Redness- a higher concentration of red blood cells in the area cause the skin to turn red, but you may not notice this in your mouth.

Heat- Like with redness, more cells moving to that area, and more movement in general will cause an increase in heat in that area. Hopefully you meds help mask this.

Swelling- The increase of blood flow to the area helps by decreasing the proportion of 'invaders' and there are also chemical signals that tell your body to send help to repair the damage. When this happens blood flow to that area increases and blood flow away from that area decreases. This causes the swelling, which sucks if you like talking or eating, or not looking like a pillow, but is also a necessary evil.

Pain- Like another user said, there are a lot of nerve endings in your mouth. Pain is caused by the swelling going on. Pain receptors are only good at detecting pain, so if they get some unusual stimulus, they just report it as pain. Think of the expression 'when all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail.' These guys only have a hammer, and the swelling in that area is pushing on them which is telling them to pound their pain hammers non-stop.

The best thing to do for inflammation is RICE. Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation. Keep drinking fluids if you can, maybe try an ice pack to help with the swelling and pain but definitely keep taking your meds. The vomiting might be from the anesthesia or just from your body being pissed off, but if it keeps up, give your dentist a call and see what he recommends. Hope this helps and feel better soon!
